verdict: Coinbase swung to a $359M net loss as revenue fell 19% to $1.22B in a soft crypto market — $209M of paper losses on the crypto it holds as an investment and a $52M restructuring charge dug the hole, even as the core business stayed Adjusted-EBITDA positive for a 14th straight quarter.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago — a soft crypto market

kpis.label: Investment losses
kpis.note: paper losses on crypto held for investment

segments.name: Transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees from crypto trading — consumer $452M, institutional $100M, other $47M. Consumer fell with spot volumes; institutional grew after the Deribit acquisition.

segments.name: Subscription and services
segments.note: Steadier income: stablecoin revenue $292M, blockchain rewards $83M, interest and finance fees $66M, and other services $114M.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Interest earned on Coinbase's own corporate cash — smaller as balances and rates fell.

opex.name: Technology & development
opex.note: Building the platform — the biggest running cost, though down 10% from Q1 after headcount cuts.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, compliance and the back office. Shown net of $10M of other operating income Coinbase reports as a negative expense.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: One-off cost of the restructuring plan announced in May 2026 — severance and related charges as Coinbase realigned its cost base.

opex.name: Crypto losses (operations)
opex.note: Paper losses on crypto Coinbase holds to run its business (staking, payments) — marked to market every quarter.

otherDetail: A $209M loss on crypto assets Coinbase holds as an investment, plus $50M of other losses (mainly marks on other investments) and $23M of interest expense.
follow100Note: Of every $100 Coinbase took in, $17.17 of the damage was paper losses on crypto it holds as an investment — non-cash marks that reverse if crypto prices recover. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Trading slowed with the market
takeaways.text: Transaction revenue fell 22% year over year to $599M as crypto spot volumes shrank. Subscriptions and services — 48% of net revenue — fell only 12%, cushioning the downturn.

takeaways.title: Paper losses on Coinbase's own crypto
takeaways.text: A year ago this line was a $362M gain; this quarter the crypto Coinbase holds as an investment lost $209M on paper. That one swing is bigger than half the net loss.

takeaways.title: The core business still earned its keep
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was positive for the 14th straight quarter at $208M, and total operating expenses fell 12% year over year as Coinbase cut costs to match the quieter market.

oneTimers: A $209M mark-to-market loss on crypto assets held for investment (versus a $362M gain a year ago) — non-cash, and it reverses if crypto prices rise.
A $52M restructuring charge from the plan announced in May 2026 to realign the cost base — severance and related one-off costs.
Losses of $32M on crypto held for operations, also mark-to-market.
footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. The quarter was a loss, so the slate 'Covered by cash on hand' block is the $359M net loss, funded from Coinbase's balance sheet. Figures are from Coinbase's Q2 2026 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.
